Far Cry 4 is an awesome game — at least, from what I could tell. The visuals are stunning, the gameplay feels smooth and exciting, and the world of Kyrat is rich with detail and action. I was genuinely excited to dive into the story and experience everything this game has to offer.

But there’s one big problem: for some reason, it only runs in Russian for me. And I don’t speak Russian.

I really wanted to enjoy the story and understand the characters, but instead, I had to guess what was happening half the time. It’s super frustrating when you’re totally into a game, but the language barrier keeps you from fully experiencing it. I couldn’t even figure out some of the missions or settings without Googling translations.

So while I liked what I could play, I can’t give it five stars until there’s an easy way to change the language or subtitles. If you understand Russian, you’ll probably love this. If not, be ready for a confusing (but still fun) ride.

For newcomers to the series, Far Cry 4 has a lot of fun, bombastic action and does the whole power fantasy of overthrowing the tyrants quite well. So if you want to fulfill your inner revolutionary fantasies or just want to have fun shooting down the bad guys, this game can be worth it. 

For those returning from Far Cry 3, if you liked what you played in that game, so much so that you want to experience it again without replaying the same game, then again Far Cry 4 could be what you're looking for. 

Got to say, Far Cry 4 feels very similar to it's predecessor to the point of almost feeling like a Nepalese modification of Far Cry 3. The gameplay is the same, from the outposts and towers to the shooting and combat, to the way the UI looks, like the collectible icons etc.  

Fallout 3 and New Vegas, if you've played them, were like this too but were very different games with their approach to the story, with factions and side content and such. Meanwhile Far Cry 4 so far is beat for story beat the same game as 3 lmao. Instead of the pirates you have the royal tyrants. The rebels were Rakyat and now they're Golden Path. The goal of both the games are the same, helping the rebels overthrow the tyrants. Even Jason and Ajay started off the same, though Ajay got over his nervous phase quicker. 

Not to mistake this as criticism necessarily. While I do think it's perhaps bit too similar, I am having fun with the game. And the mountainous Kyrat is beautiful though somehow bit similar to the tropical Rook islands again. 

If you played Far Cry 3 but feel you've had your fill of the game, and want a newer/different experience, 4 might not be it for you imo. But if you're looking for more of the same but with different settings and characters, or if you're new and want to start from 4 than 5 or 6, then 4 could be fun times.

I recently replayed Far Cry 4, and honestly, it’s still one of the most fun open-world shooters I’ve played. The game puts you in the shoes of Ajay Ghale, a guy returning to his homeland, Kyrat, which is basically a fictional version of Nepal. Things quickly go south when he gets caught in the middle of a civil war between rebels and a flamboyant dictator named Pagan Min.

The world is absolutely stunning — snowy mountains, dense forests, small villages — it really feels alive. You can hunt animals, climb towers, or just drive around listening to local radio. It’s one of those games where you might start doing one mission and then get distracted for an hour by random side stuff.
Combat feels great. There’s a huge variety of weapons and vehicles — even elephants you can ride into battle (which never gets old). The stealth system works nicely too; you can sneak around with a bow or just go full chaos with grenades and machine guns

The story isn’t super deep, but it’s interesting enough. Pagan Min steals the show — he’s stylish, sarcastic, and a bit crazy, but in a fun way. The rebels, though, can feel a bit one-dimensional. Still, there are moments that make you think about morality and choices

What can I say, if you've played an Ubisoft shooter or even action/adventure open world, you know what you're going to get. It is what it is, mindless running around, collecting, unlocking, and shooting stuff. 

It has a very silly story attached to it. I mean, the main character says at the start "I'm not a soldier, but I'll help where I can", next minute is tearing through soldiers with an AK like it is second nature. But you don't play Farcry for the 'in depth, genius' story writing. You play for the the mindless shooty shooty fun, and Farcry 4 scratches the itch. However, just like Farcry 3, the weapons really don't have much wait to them and everything can get rather repetitive quick. Or tedious if you take the eagles into account (yes, the eagles are as annoying as everyone says).

Far Cry 4 feels like an extended version of Far Cry 3 but with smoother gameplay, better graphics and much more atmosphere. I already platinumed the PS3 version of this game when I was a kid and after 4 years, replaying it now hits with pure nostalgia. The main missions are good, the choices actually matter, and choosing between Sabal or Amita feels like walking on a tightrope. (Amita is still a bi#ch btw.)

Pagan Min is a TOP TIER villain

Pagan Min feels like a more elegant, calm, and active version of Vaas. Throughout the game he randomly calls Ajay and talks about memories with his mother. It’s creepy in a fun way, almost like he’s always watching you from somewhere. Vaas may be iconic, but Pagan Min is just as memorable—maybe even better.

Ajay Ghale – Decent Protagonist

Ajay doesn’t feel very different from Jason Brody, but at least he talks, reacts and has some personality during dialogues. For a Far Cry protagonist, that’s honestly enough.

Graphics & Atmosphere

For a 2014 game, the graphics are still beautiful in 2025.

Kyrat is one of the best open-world maps in the Far Cry series.

Environments look detailed and alive.

Story & Missions

Storytelling and missions are better compared to Far Cry 3. Some missions feel like they came straight out of a thriller movie. Ubisoft actually cooked with this one.

Crafting & Progression

At first, I thought crafting would be as painful as in Far Cry 3 (I spent 4 hours hunting just for upgrades there), but crafting in Far Cry 4 is more balanced and fun. Hunting doesn’t feel like a chore anymore.

Stealth & Signature Weapons

Progression is linked to signature weapons this time instead of a pure skill tree grind. It actually feels rewarding.

(bow and sniper is enough for me lol)

Stealth mechanics are improved compared to FC3 Dragging bodies, vertical takedowns. The additions were good. But I really miss the Double Death From Above takedown from FC3

Co-op & DLCs

Sadly, I didn’t have a friend to play co-op with and never had the DLCs on PS3, but I watched both from youtube so here's my opinion about dlc's.

Escape from Durgesh: Dominate Kyrat before the timer ends

Valley of the Yetis: Pure chaos (ending was wild ngl. for a child at the age of 12 seeing that ending is scared the shi out of me a bit)

The only thing I didn’t like

Being forced into an Indian bloodline story and "protect these people, OUR FAMILY, My Brother im always here for you." type of narrative felt unnecessary.

The Result

✔ Great Main Villain
✔ Amazing open world
✔ Still fun in 2025
✔ Solid story and missions
✔ Great gameplay loop

Ubisoft really needs to stop forcing their launcher and overlay into everything. I hate that you can’t even play Far Cry 4 without going through their stuff, and even when you leave the overlay on like they want, it doesn’t tell you what it’s actually doing. I kept unlocking things with zero explanation of what they were or if I even got anything. The worst part was launching the game: there are about five loud intro videos you can’t skip, and they’re way more obnoxious than anything in the game itself. On top of that, I couldn’t play in borderless windowed mode. Every time I tried, the game would open zoomed in way past my screen size, even set to 1080p on a 4K monitor. I could only see a corner of the screen and didn’t feel like wasting time troubleshooting something no other game does.

And now for my attempt at a spoiler-free review:

Far Cry 4 is still a good time. I liked being able to choose who was in control during the story, even if I’m not sure it really changes much. There’s a unique alternate ending early on, which was a cool touch. The main villain was alright, but I didn’t really care much about him. It felt like most of the time he was just talking at you, which got old after a while. I also wish one of the major characters had a choice moment like the others, but instead it just ends with no input from you.

There’s a good amount to do outside the main missions. The variance in side missions helps keep things from getting too repetitive, and the karma system adds extra stuff to do while you're moving from place to place, especially if you're on foot. I liked that enemy soldiers still roam the world even after you capture outposts, and the radio changes based on which towers you've freed, which was a nice touch. The fortress and retaliation system is cool too, but if you clear everything too early like I did, you end up missing most of the retaliation events.

The gyrocopter was a fun addition, but trying to do takeouts or get the achievement for it on PC was weird. Even worse, changing the copter controls also messes with your on-foot and driving controls, which shouldn’t happen. Elephant riding was cool, but I only used it for the achievement. The auto-drive feature came in handy when I didn’t feel like driving myself. As for the online achievements, they’re pretty much impossible now because nobody plays those modes anymore, and there’s no way to play them with bots. I’m not going to sit around every day waiting for a bunch of people to show up online just to unlock a few achievements.

The characters were good and had some unique storylines, especially the side characters, but they just weren’t really for me. One of them quoted religious stuff while talking about weapons, which was creative, but I didn’t care for him. Another pair of characters had a completely different vibe that worked, but also wasn’t my thing. Most of them were solid overall, just not the kind of people I felt like sticking with beyond what I needed for skills or trophies.

[h1]Far Cry 4 Review[/h1]

[hr]
[h1]Overview[/h1]
A solid Far Cry that does exactly what you expect. It looks good, plays fine, and gives you a big checklist playground. It does not meaningfully push the series forward, but if you like the loop you will have a good time.

[hr]
[h1]What It Is[/h1]
You are Ajay Ghale returning to Kyrat, a Himalayan nation torn between Pagan Min’s regime and a rebel faction. You liberate outposts and fortresses, hunt wildlife to upgrade gear, collect resources, and choose how to help the resistance while the story nudges you between key missions.

[hr]
[h1]World and Atmosphere[/h1]
Kyrat is beautiful and varied. Snowy peaks, forest valleys, hilltop shrines, and cliff roads feel alive with civilians, patrols, wildlife, and random skirmishes. The map size is just right for roaming. Radio towers and viewpoints deliver great vistas. Visuals hold up well for the era.

[hr]
[h1]Combat and Tools[/h1]
Gunplay is competent. Bows, ARs, SMGs, LMGs, shotguns, pistols, and a few signature guns cover most styles. Stealth with takedowns, bait, and alarms feels familiar from Far Cry 3. Nothing wildly new, but it works.

[hr]
[h1]Systems and Side Content[/h1]
Traditional Ubisoft mix: outposts, fortresses, hunting, races, hostage rescues, propaganda posters, collectibles. Loads to do, sometimes too much. Expect repetition if you chase 100 percent or achievements. Arena mode is fun for a bit, but grinding to rank 10 can drag. Multiplayer lobbies are mostly inactive today, so plan boosting if you care about those trophies.

[hr]
[h1]Story and Villain[/h1]
The plot is basic but serviceable. Pagan Min is the standout, a stylish and charismatic antagonist who elevates cutscenes even if he is not quite Vaas-level iconic. Faction choice moments add flavor rather than deep consequences.

[hr]
[h1]Performance and Polish[/h1]
Runs well on modern hardware for a 2014 release. Occasional jank is there, but nothing show stopping.

[hr]
[h1]What Works[/h1]
[list]
[*] Striking Himalayan setting with wildlife and constant ambient activity
[*] Satisfying stealth outpost clears and fortress assaults
[*] Big toybox of weapons and vehicles
[*] Pagan Min steals scenes and adds personality
[/list]

[hr]
[h1]What Falls Short[/h1]
[list]
[*] Feels very close to Far Cry 3 in structure and mechanics
[*] Side content gets repetitive fast if you do everything
[*] Arena grind and inactive multiplayer for achievement hunters
[/list]

[hr]
[h1]Verdict[/h1]
Recommended with expectations set. If you want a classic Far Cry loop in a gorgeous new location, Far Cry 4 delivers. If you were hoping for bold changes or a reinvention, this plays it safe. Best enjoyed by focusing on the main path with a curated slice of side activities.

Pros:

Atmosphere & World-Building: Kyrat is breathtaking. The blend of Himalayan culture, political unrest, and mythological elements gives the game a rich and immersive backdrop. The side stories and hidden lore sprinkled throughout make exploration truly rewarding.

Storytelling: The main storyline is compelling and well-paced, with an air of mystery that keeps you engaged. The moral ambiguity of your allies and enemies makes choices more impactful.

Villain: Pagan Min easily ranks among the greatest antagonists in the Far Cry series—charismatic, unpredictable, and layered. He steals every scene he’s in.

Cons:

Radio Control Limitations: While driving, I often found myself wanting to just enjoy the ambient music or local tunes—but the ever-talking RJ Rabi Ray Rana can get a bit much. Ironically, at times I wanted to hear his take on current events in Kyrat, but the background music mixed with his voice was too loud and distracting. Ubisoft really should’ve given us the option to control music and RJ volume separately—or even toggle them independently.

Bait System Flaw: Throwing bait is a cool feature, but it lacks fine control. The game doesn't let you choose which animal skin/meat to use for bait. This becomes frustrating when you're trying to conserve rare skins needed for crafting. A simple selection system could've fixed this.

When discussing the Far Cry series, we can’t overlook this installment. While Far Cry 4 didn’t revolutionize the franchise and largely followed in the footsteps of its predecessor, it’s far from a bad game. As someone who’s completed the entire series, I’d even rank Far Cry 4 in my Top 3, narrowly surpassing the legendary Far Cry 3.

Yes, Far Cry 4 faced criticism for being too similar to Far Cry 3, but in my opinion, it carves out its own identity. The immersion in Eastern culture, one of the best stories in the series, refined gameplay, and solid visuals make it stand out. Every character is vibrant and well-developed, with their own motivations and backstories. Pagan Min isn’t just a generic madman, no one here is purely good or evil. Everyone has a purpose. What I love most is how your choices matter, even in small ways, shaping the ending.

Gameplay-wise, it’s a delight. Everything Far Cry 3 did well, this one improves upon, making mechanics smoother and more intuitive. There’s also a wider arsenal of weapons and gear. Graphically, while not groundbreaking, the Ultra settings deliver stunning landscapes, perfect for screenshots, and performance is polished. I experienced zero crashes, bugs, or glitches during my playthrough.

That said, the game isn’t flawless. The AI leaves something to be desired, as both allies and enemies can be hilariously incompetent at times.

But at the end of the day, Far Cry 4 remains a game I look back on fondly, one I’ve replayed multiple times. If you’re looking for an open-world shooter to sink hours into, this is it.

[h1]Far Cry 4[/h1]

This is the 2nd game I've played and beat in the franchise. My first was Far Cry 5, I suppose I will be playing the series backwards and I guess I'll finish it off with Far Cry 6 as well as the spinoffs. Let me just say this first, this game is beautiful. The map is pretty large, the graphics still hold up, and you'll always have something to do whether that be attacking outposts, infiltrating bell towers, going through some supernatural quest by getting high with two dudes who decided to live in your dad's place, or just simply hunting animals to upgrade your gear, it's a lot of fun. 

[h2]Story[/h2]
So let me talk about the story for a moment, I will try to be as spoiler free as I can. The story in this game is absolutely amazing. It will have you making important decisions, and your choices will matter. You get plenty of decisions to make and all of which will lead into pretty much the same ending although the way you get to the end is greatly changed. The campaign is also pretty long, at least it was for me. Took me about 25 hours to get through it all, I skipped a lot of things just so I could finish the game up and maybe come back to it if I wanted to. 
The main antagonist, (or so the one the game wants you to believe) is Pagan Min. He rules over the land of Kyrat and honestly is a pretty fun guy and a great villain at that. He plays a pretty important role in the overall story and all but I won't get into all that here.

[h2]Optimization[/h2]
I played most of this on my PC but recently I've gotten a Steam Deck and the last 3 hours have been on the Steam Deck. It doesn't run completely perfect on it but by tweaking many settings you can play at a pretty stable 40-60 fps on the Steam Deck which is not bad at all. For PC and pretty much everything else, this game has great optimization.

The game also includes smaller objects and places that provide information about the world and its history, which helps build the setting in a deeper way.

The visual quality of the game is high, with natural colors, good lighting, and detailed textures. The changing time of day also affects how the world looks. The music syncs nice and changes with the action, supporting the mood of each part of the game. 

Overall, Far Cry 4 is a well-designed game that offers solid gameplay, strong setting, and rich sound and graphics.

[h3]LONG[/h3]

Far Cry 4 is a very interesting first-person sandbox, with an emphasis on action and stealth.

The gameplay is very fun and everything works well, I don't recall experiencing any bugs. The variety of weapons allows you to play explosively or completely stealthily, whichever you prefer. The enemies are a bit repetitive but satisfactory for this type of game.

The artistic features are good, but not extraordinary. The story is cool and keeps you interested until the end. The map is very pretty and feels alive, and the random interactions happen very organically. The soundtrack is good, well calibrated for the style of the game and complements the scenery and dialogues well.

Overall, it's a game that has aged very well. For a game that's over 10 years old, it's fun, beautiful, and well-made. It took me 46 hours to finish the game and get all the achievements. There are some achievements that are hard to get due to the game's old engine and the low number of players in multiplayer.

Do I recommend it? Yes! But the game is definitely not worth the full price, the good news is that it's often 80% or more off.

Far Cry 4 is an exciting open-world action-adventure shooter that captivates you from the very first minutes with its atmosphere and scale. The story takes place in the fictional region of Kyrat, inspired by the Himalayas, where the protagonist gets caught in the conflict between the dictator Pagan Min and the rebels.
The game world is incredibly beautiful and alive — mountains, jungles, rivers, and villages are detailed down to the smallest elements. The best part is the complete freedom of action: explore, hunt, complete missions in different ways, capture outposts, or ride an elephant! For me, riding elephants and flying the gyrocopter were pure thrills.
The story isn’t very deep, but thanks to the charismatic villain Pagan Min and vivid characters, it remains memorable and engaging. The gameplay is dynamic and varied — you can play stealthily or storm in with guns blazing.
The game truly makes you live in this world, not just complete missions. It left a strong impression on me, and I often returned to Kyrat just to wander around and enjoy the atmosphere.
Conclusion:
Far Cry 4 is an exciting and vibrant world that delivers genuine enjoyment. It perfectly balances freedom and story, leaving only positive impressions behind.

If you have any issues running the game or with freezing etc. follow these instructions and it should solve most issues:

1) Run the game
2) Ctrl + Alt + Del -> Task Manager -> Details
3) Find FarCry4.exe in the list
4) Right click -> Set Affinity
5) Unselect all processor cores except your last 4. For example if you have cores 0-11, unselect all except 8, 9, 10, and 11
6) Apply changes and then go back to your already open game

Your game should now run smoothly!

P.S. You will have to do this every time you play, luckily it's very quick and easy to do

Far Cry 4 is mechanically a big improvement over Far Cry 3 — I was honestly surprised by how much smoother and more refined everything feels. The auto-drive feature is a great addition, and the UI/menus show a clear improvement in usability and polish. Also, the game’s art direction is stunning. Massive kudos to the artists!

However, the setting and overall vibe still feel a bit too similar to Far Cry 3. I wish the theme and environment were more distinct — sometimes it felt like I was still in the same game.

The missions can be very difficult, and in some cases, it's not clear what you're supposed to do. The constant attacks from wild animals make things even more intense, which might not be everyone’s cup of tea. Also, not being able to pause cutscenes is a major downside.

The Buzzer (mini helicopter) is fun, but the altitude limit is frustrating, especially when trying to complete certain objectives.

Unfortunately, the final mission was underwhelming — I was expecting something much more epic to close the story.

While there’s a decent variety of content, the side quests eventually become very repetitive by the end of the game.

Overall, it’s a great game, especially if you liked Far Cry 3 — just don’t expect a drastically different experience.

[h1]Review of Far Cry 4[/h1] 
I'll never forget the level of excitement that consumed me leading up to Far Cry 4's release. To this day, I'd consider myself a pretty big fan of the Ubisoft Far Cry series. My favorite game tends to bounce between a couple, but it's almost consistently always been Far Cry 4. Even though the game launched to great success, and many have come to appreciate it years later, I feel as though it often gets overshadowed by Far Cry 3. 

While FC3 was a big deal, and is a game I also love, referring to Far Cry 4 with the unfortunate and lazy argument of "Copy/Paste" is not only unfair, but completely asinine. It did what any good sequel should do. Took a now well established formula, refined the parts that needed work. Spiced up the existing bits, and expanded upon it with new content.

[u]A Mother's Dying Wish (Story)[/u]
The plot of FC4 puts you into the shoes of Ajay Ghale. Who's traveling to his birth country of Kyrat high in the Himalayan Mountains. Based on the real world locations of Nepal & Tibet (I believe?). Ajay's mother wished to have her ashes returned to "Lakshmana", though exactly what or where this is was never conveyed. Upon arriving, Ajay finds himself being thrust into a civil war between the Golden Path & the country's ruler Pagan Min, and his Royalists. 

I won't deny that Pagan Min is one of, if not just outright, my favorite atagonists in the series. Even if, like usual, he's underutilized. You see, to make a good villain that's also interesting, is to humanize them. Their goals may be noble, and their heart may be in the right place. However their methods may be morally dubious. Not only does Pagan seem to want what's best for Kyrat, but he also seems to care a lot about Ajay. As it turns out, your parents, the Golden Path, and Pagan Min, all share a common history. Let's not forget just how charismatic Pagan is. 

Far Cry 4 has multiple endings, with variations throughout them depending on smaller choices made during your playthrough. While progressing, you'll need to side with one of two leaders in the Golden Path. Amita & or Sabal. Each has their own vision for the future of Kyrat. Your decisions will lead to not only alternative missions & objectives, but the outcome of multiple character's fates. Of course FC4 is also known for its "Secret" ending, which can be obtained in the opening minutes of the prologue. Amita & Sabal are insufferable at times. Though this is intentional.

[u]Welcome to Kyrat (Gameplay & Setting)[/u]
Many people tend to forget, that a lot of the series' staples were birthed right here in FC4. Sure, plenty of them are further expanded upon in later titles, but the roots are within this game. A flyable aircraft. Early 'Guns for Hire' system. Animal companion mechanics. Rideable animals. Antagonist "Lieutenants". Cooperative play. More diverse & improved takedowns. The grappling hook, and more.
|
In comparison to the previous game, FC4 is much larger in terms of content & variety. This time around we have maybe 4-5 times the amount of different secondary quests, some of which have their own character's and mini-stories. Alongside the main story, you'll also be able to hunt down blood diamonds for Longinous, test out new drugs for Yogi & Reggie, or explore Shangri-La through the eyes of Kalinag. An arena with its own progression & challenges. Random world events that increase your Karma for additional rewards. Hundreds of collectibles, some of which unlock readable entries. Scattered notes to learn more about Kyrat and its people. A majority of the weaponry from the third game return, with an added roster of entirely new toys to play around with. Including my absolute favorite, the MG42. With DLC, you'll also be able to take on a Hurk related questline & multiple standalone missions. Many of which send you up in to the freezing cold summits of the Himalayas. I could go on.

I'd like to mention Fortresses as well. They're massive strongholds, one for each of the antagonists. The idea is that they become weaker once you've defeated their commander. These are amazingly fun, but seemingly unique only to this game. They also have a feature where Royalists will try to retake captured outposts in a region, until that region's fortress has been taken down. 

Kyrat itself is a lot more dense than previous play areas. Considering there's no ocean here. Instead, the game makes use of verticality much more. This being a breeze thanks to the new grappling hook utility. The Pacific islands from FC3 are gorgeous, but I will never be able to keep my jaw from dropping when you see that impressive backdrop of the snow capped mountains that surround Kyrat. Split between a Northern & Southern territory, with lots of beautiful scenery.

[u]Visuals & OST[/u]
Visually, Far Cry 4's fidelity is a step up. Especially in regards to lighting. However the visual styles of Kyrat & its culture is distinctly different to that of FC3. The audio in the game is great. Weapons sound heavy and powerful. The forest ambience lets you get lost in its virtual space. 

I don't think FC4's soundtrack comes even close to the amazing OST from FC3. That's not to say there isn't some great tracks here though. Such as the Shangri-La finale boss theme. 

[u]Frustrations[/u]
With all the good, there's naturally some ugly. Most of these issues got on my nerves, but are small enough to not ruin the overall experience. FC4 is filled with exotic wild animals. However, these are either too common, or too aggressive. Dholes & Wolves are especially obnoxious. You'll get jumped by a Leopard, walk 20 feet and get attacked by a pack of wolves, walk 20 feet and get latched by an eagle, walk 20 feet and get attacked by another pack of wolves. The problem with eagles, is that they force you into an animation where they grab your arm. But this animation happens 100% of the time, and triggers when they're still diving on you. Giving you very little time you kill it before being forced to take 75% of your health in damage because a couple talons poked your arm.

Toss in some crashes during the racing activities. Some grapple spots that wouldn't register. Undiscovered locations that have really annoying sweet spots to trigger as being explored. Horrible auto drive system that throws off aim. Enemies either not seeing you five feet in front of them, or spotting you through trees from a mile away. Bow wielding enemies firing with perfect accuracy on the move. The wing suit deploying when simply trying to jump between gaps. Etc. Aside from these issues I had, Far Cry 4 is an absolute blast. 

[h1]Conclusion (Pros & Cons)[/h1]
I hope that if you've ever put off playing Far Cry 4, you'll give it a chance. Whether you're a fan of Far Cry or Open World games in general, it's well worth it in my opinion. Although I'm quite familiar with the game, it took roughly 25.5 hours to 100% the game on the hardest difficulty for this review. You can get more content in the form of the standalone DLC's Escape From Durgesh and the expansion pack that is Valley of the Yeti. There's also a map editor & competitive multiplayer.

It was one of the first games I played on my PlayStation 4 back in the day. I replayed it recently, about ten years later, and it’s just as fun as I remembered, maybe even more so.

First of all, Kyrat is beautiful, and I mean beautiful. This game doesn’t look like it’s from 2014. The views are breathtaking, and the setting feels truly unique. It really makes you feel like an outsider in a foreign land.

The gunplay is solid. There’s a wide variety of weapons to try out, but truth be told, I stuck with just a few favorites for most of the game.

There’s also a ton of side content to do. I genuinely enjoyed 100%ing the game, but I’d be lying if I said I didn’t feel a bit of fatigue after collecting my 40th mask, tearing down my 130th poster, or repeating yet another side mission.

The voice acting is phenomenal, especially after making story choices. I actually felt bad after siding with Sabal once, thanks to the amazing performance by Amita’s voice actress. That said, it’s a bit questionable that the characters reveal their true motives and tell you how badly you messed up after you’ve already made your choice.

Pagan Min is wonderful. He’s charismatic, funny, and I always enjoyed listening to him whenever he showed up, same goes for several of the other characters.

The story is solid overall, though there’s one part at the airport that I didn’t really care about. It could’ve been handled or explained differently.

The Arena is fun, but grinding it to rank 10 for the unique weapon was definitely tedious.

I also tried the multiplayer for the achievement  it’s pretty much dead, but I’m not surprised, since it didn’t seem particularly interesting.

All in all, I can highly recommend this game. It’s my favorite Far Cry title, and I’ll definitely revisit it again at some point in the future.

When listing favorite Far Cry games, you might mention 3, 5, or even, God forbid, the 6th installment, but not the fourth. And it's all about the antagonist!

Vaas, Joseph Seed, Castillo… They are so charismatic that FOR THEM, you play the game. And the last one is so cool that many were willing to pay up to 70 bucks for zoomer crap just to meet him.

Now, what about the bleached blond guy? What can you remember about him?

Disclaimer: we're going to lay down the facts about Far Cry. It might get stuffy for the kids and the challenged ones. It's better to open a window for some fresh air right away.

ALL Ubisoft games of the last 10 years are built on one concept.

    They introduce you to your friends, show the enemy, show why he's bad.
    Then they throw you into a pit called "Endless mini-missions in an open world to summon a boss."

If it were a fantasy or Souls game, I would say, "Well, it's an RPG, you have to level up."

But is Far Cry an RPG? For those who are not aware, RPG implies a tabletop role-playing game, or as they say colloquially, a tabletop! If anyone's interested, go to YouTube and watch the evolution of RPG games.
And, of course, RPG doesn't just imply character leveling up, but a gradual advantage that you can gain through mini-duels, which will give you an edge by the end of the game!
Example? Any part of tabletop games where you can level up and break the face of another boss with one blow.
Correct, this is done for the serfs who heard the word RPG in the Dota chat one day. The second time when they were yelled at in Minecraft. And a day later, they went to Google to see what your RPG is, went to Steam, found Far Cry, and bought it on torrent trackers.

In other words, with this little flaw, the developers lowered the entry threshold (into your mom).

Now, what about Far Cry? Here RPG is for the sake of RPG, and missions for the sake of running time. Because of the impotence of the writers or laziness? - a rhetorical question.
Go milk cows or collect manure to accumulate the required amount of reputation points to summon a boss. This stupid RPG is what we deserved. Hello Dying Light 2 and goose presentations.
"This is an RPG!" one of the readers of this review will caw. No, this is not an RPG, - I will answer.

An acceptable example of RPG NOT in a tabletop game is Cyberpunk 2077.

In general, the marketing department and executive directors of Ubisoft are just geniuses who changed the whole industry. They took the concept of blacklist and turned it into garbage, and even added an RPG tag.

Now again, for the gifted. Ubisoft took a game with a cat-poop scenario and stuffed it with mini-missions up to the top! And this gave them exactly a smooth surface for stamping games on it. Soon, from garage garbage collectors to other companies, everyone picked up this concept, and it became the canon for RPG games.
And you won't finish it! The game has an RPG tag, half the country doesn't even know that it's not the same as an MMO. And the other half is sure that character leveling equals a role-playing game, and screw the fact that there are no roles, and in the case of Far Cry, the protagonist is mute!

With such a "given," it's not surprising that Far Cry 4 became absolutely mediocre and faceless crap. And what carried this franchise on its shoulders, suddenly turned out that besides the clay "bow" and one hundred percent botoxed boobs, it couldn't offer anything else.

[h3][u]TL/DR: If you own an ultrawide [b]do not buy[/b][/u][/h3]

This was one of my favorite games growing up so upon seeing it on sale (I can't even remember when) I quickly nabbed it while it was cheap. Like oh so many mega-sale impulse buys it has sat in my library untouched waiting for it's day in the sun. I'd recently seen a video on youtube which reignited my interests in the game and so around 12 hours ago I decided to take a trip down memory lane and downloaded it. Initial impressions were positive - even after a decade the game still holds its own in terms of graphics and audio. Overall I was pleased, but there were a few problems. 

The first problem is the lack of a skip button, a problem which only gets worse the more you restart the game to troubleshoot. Not too big, but still an issue. The other and more fatal problem is the FOV. The FOV on ultrawide monitors is absolutely horrendous. It's like you have binoculars glued to your face, you're constantly zoomed in and you can't change it. This problem is exclusive to ultrawide monitors as there [b]is[/b] an FOV slider, it's just disabled for 21:9 aspect ratios. You can change the aspect ratio in settings thus allowing you to change the FOV but this isn't a fix. 
Changing the ratio while in fullscreen results in the window stretching to fill the screen.
Changing the ratio in borderless results in the window ballooning in size where you can only see the top left corner of the game.
And changing it while windowed works but doesn't bind the cursor to the game. Just looking around results in the cursor flying around the screen and single click pulls you out of the game.
Quite literally unplayable.

The thing that drove me to write this review is that I just can't understand why. I could only think of two possibilities, but neither hold up to scrutiny.
The first possibility is that Ubi considers it unbalanced. The same FOV value on a wider screen would allow you to see more than otherwise intended.... except we don't all use the same FOV value. If balance was the reason there wouldn't be an FOV option in the first place. The largest FOV on 16:9 also allows you to see several times more than 21:9. It also doesn't make sense to 'balance' visibility for a game that is first and foremost a single player game, and even if it wasn't it still wouldn't excuse the resulting unplayability.
The other possibility was that it breaks the game, but it just doesn't. There used to be a workaround where editing a single hex value in one of the file would unlock the FOV slider. I was unable to try this but from what I could find there were zero issues - the game ran completely normally. This popular fix (which had existed for 5+ years) was either broken or outright patched in the most recent update, and I suspect it was the latter rather than the former.

My best guess as to the real reasoning behind this decision is to bolster the ego of some manager at Ubi.

[b]Thus far I have spent 5+ hours troubleshooting
1.5 hours writing this review
15 minutes watching cutscenes
5 minutes of actual gameplay
and have enjoyed practically none of it. 
All this just because of an issue that has existed for as long as ultrawides have, but one that should have never existed in the first place. 
Thanks Ubi[/b]

Far Cry 4 Review: Fun Gameplay Undermined by Shallow Systems

Far Cry 4 is an undeniably fun game to play, boasting improved mechanics and an expansive, vibrant world that feels alive. However, it falls short of being truly memorable due to its lackluster progression systems, an uninspired narrative, and missed opportunities in its design.

The core gameplay—gunplay, driving, and using tools like the grappling hook—has been refined and polished since Far Cry 3. Combat encounters are fluid, with ample ways to approach objectives, and the dynamic world can lead to spontaneous and exciting skirmishes. Kyrat, the fictional Himalayan setting, is breathtaking, with its lush forests, snow-capped peaks, and teeming wildlife. Yet, as you play, it becomes clear that this vast world is more of a hollow shell than a true sandbox.

Exploration is one of the biggest disappointments. While Kyrat feels dynamic, the rewards for venturing off the beaten path are almost nonexistent. Looting becomes a repetitive chore, offering little excitement or meaningful progression. What’s the point of exploring when there’s no tangible payoff?

The progression system suffers from being overly simplified, reducing skills to uninspired perks that fail to provide a sense of growth or mastery. Even more frustrating is the game’s broken economy. Players are never restricted in what guns they can purchase, making early decisions meaningless. The attachment system, which could have added depth to weapon customization, is puzzlingly limited—each weapon is restricted to one attachment or none at all. This raises the question: why include customization at all if it’s so underwhelming?

Far Cry 4’s narrative also leaves much to be desired. While Pagan Min is a charismatic antagonist, the story lacks emotional weight and memorable twists. The moral choices presented feel shallow and have little impact on the overall experience, leaving players disengaged from the tale.

It’s a shame because the gameplay mechanics are vastly improved, and Kyrat’s setting feels unique in the gaming landscape. Far Cry 4 could have been a standout entry in the series, but its unrewarding systems and missed opportunities hold it back from greatness. It’s a fun ride, but one that ultimately feels hollow.

With Far Cry 3 being as outstanding as it is, it would be unfair to call its successor bad for trying to imitate it. The fact of the matter is, however, you are better off sticking to 3 or advancing to further titles. There are little to no story connections, and 4 hardly has any improvements over 3. To add to that, the protagonist has no recognizable development, the so-called moral choices are exaggerated at best, and the open world, while beautiful at a distance, is bland and lacking in variety.

But, if you find yourself interested in certain things, there are exceptions. I would say it'd be worth buying on sale if you've got the file storage to spare for at least as long as it takes to finish it, IF:
- you're interested in Northern Indian/Nepalese culture, style, and folktale
- you want to ride an elephant
- you're interested in solid villains -- Pagan Min is very interesting, but he's basically just Handsome Jack without the PreSequel backstory
- you prefer forested mountains over an island jungle

Far Cry 4 is exactly the same as Far Cry 3...

...but significantly worse in almost every way. 

Never in my 15+ years of playing video games, has a game ever made me say out loud "please stop, this isn't fun", quite this often. It's really and truly THAT bad. 

Let's start with Freedom. This is something that FC4 constantly removes from the player. You have no freedom to do whatever you want, and it's been very frustrating for me. I think of a way to do something, and does it work? No, no it doesn't. 

I can't shoot anyone because this mission is mandatory stealth, if someone sees me I instantly lose the mission. 
I can't stealth in the particular way that I want to, for the same reason. If someone sees me, I instantly lose. There are more ways than one to do stealth. 
I gained access to the northern part of the country, and now it's impossible to do my favorite way of capturing missions - turreted trucks - because there's guaranteed to be multiple enemies carrying rocket launchers now. I instantly die.
I can't melee any enemies because each and every single time I get close to them, they bash me with their gun and I get stun locked. I literally can't do anything, get shot, and die. 
And now, just plain shooting someone has become a huge headache because the moment I get nicked by a single bullet, my entire camera shifts upwards, ruining my aim.

I can't even go anywhere I want sometimes, it keeps telling me I'm going out of bounds when I'm very clearly not. The player should be allowed to go anywhere they want to, whenever they want to. Just don't activate the main missions in that area.

Stealth is atrocious. 

If you shoot someone with a silenced weapon, and you miss, oh well... Every enemy NPC becomes superhuman. They know the exact location the shot came from, they look in your direction, they see you from ludicrously far away, AND THEY CAN SEE YOU THROUGH OBJECTS. 

Trees, vehicles, in one case an entire wall, I have gotten seen when I absolutely should not have. They even try to shoot through the same solid objects they see you through, most noticeably trees. Not only is this a problem, but during their superhuman status, they will also notice you extremely quickly. That little "vision bar" fills up nearly instantly, if not literally instantly, if you're in their ginormous field of view.

I tried to force my preferred way of stealth - Loud Stealth, which is using noise and dead bodies to attract enemies away from my position - and it took me two entire hours and I didn't even completely do it. It saved my progress of saving the slaves, but it didn't save any progress I made killing the enemy. The checkpoints in this game are some of the worst I've ever seen, and this is a horrifically beautiful example of how. If I kill people and save a slave, it should also save all the enemies I killed. Basic checkpoint design.

The weapons in this game are better balanced than they were in Far Cry 3, but it doesn't solve the issue that the ones you unlock earliest in the game are pretty much the best weapons you'll have for the rest of the game. It took me all the way to unlocking nearly every single weapon in the game, and there was only 1 weapon for each of my 4 slots I've found to be better than what I immediately had access to from the beginning of the game. This is not okay. Things I unlock, should be better than what I started with.

The graphics are messed up and I can't understand why. There's a forced blur on weapons, and I have absolutely no way of disabling it at all. I've tried following online guides, nothing works anymore. Just nothing. It looks like sh*t. That's not the worst of it, the worst would absolutely be the fact that the game's lighting on weapons is unbelievably bad. I can't enjoy the way my gun looks because it constantly has a shadow casted on it, making almost the entire gun black. I just can't see it, arguably making it a waste of money for me to have bought that skin for it.

The wingsuit is a very good item in concept, but executed awfully in FC4. You press, OR HOLD shift to activate it. HOLD?! YOU CAN HOLD SHIFT?! WHAT???

If you're confused...

When you run and jump, you instinctively HOLD SHIFT during the duration of the jump, don't you? You hold the run button? IT ACTIVATES THE F*CKING WINGSUIT, AND YOU FLY STRAIGHT INTO A WALL AND IMMEDIATELY DIE. Or get needlessly hurt really badly. 

Far Cry 4 also has the exact same problem that Far Cry 3 has - You're not allowed to choose whether you want to physically heal yourself, or use a healing syringe. If I want to heal, no matter what, I use the healing syringe. I am missing 1 bar of health, I don't want to use an item that heals 6 bars of HP to fix that. 

Sometimes when I walk away from an outpost, it instantly starts getting attacked and now I'm forcefully roped into a mission of having to defend the outpost. These suck balls, there are way too many enemies literally everywhere and all I do is die repeatedly in my sad attempts to defend my outpost. I eventually win, but only after dying 5 or so times. It's so stupid it hurts.

Oh, and I can't forget this: Friendly NPCs LOVE to run DIRECTLY in front of your car, you hit them, AND THE GAME PUNISHES YOU FOR IT. IT WASN'T MY FAULT. THEY RAN IN FRONT OF ME... But this never happens with enemy NPCs. They always perfectly run out of the way. So what the hell, are the friendly NPCs just suicidal? God, I don't get it. 

The only genuine improvement that Far Cry 4 has over Far Cry 3, is that the whole place doesn't magically become completely safe after capturing an outpost. There are still enemies roaming around and actually giving you something to do instead of being bored.
It's boring - I may be to odd man out here I love the Far Cry franchise but this one is NOT fun.

The fact publishers can remove and censor content from a product already purchased over 10 years ago is not something we should ignore until it becomes normalised in this industry, should straight up be illegal.

Edit: Apparently this has since been reversed, which is a relief - they claim a mistake but I'm sadly not that trusting anymore.

I could not bring myself to finish it.

Boy, what a slog. I've done my time in the Ubislop mines, played other FC titles, AC games, etc. but this is one of the few games I felt I was absolutely forcing myself through.

The good: The overarching story, on paper, is interesting and solid. This is implemented poorly in practice. There's a thread of mysticism, which is in line with (the quite good) FC3 and adds a little je nais se quois. This is implemented poorly in practice. The shooting and driving are both arcade-y, and fun. There's a variety of weapons which are unlocked through a reasonable range of activities. New guns you couldn't previously see/unlock populate into your store, which I really appreciate. I hate seeing all my options at the very start. Climbing was also fun, and felt appropriate for the setting... but this is only a small mechanic.

The bad: Woof, well. The wingsuit+parachute feel awful, unwieldy, and useless, expecially coupled with a brutally small health pool and insane fall/impact damage. On KB+M, the sprint control also deploys the wingsuit, which means god forbid you try to run off or vault a higher ledge. You will launch, wingsuit, and crash, leading to a mystifyingly long loading screen. Seriously - does the game handle resetting things after player death weirdly? Why are death screens so much longer? 

The story sounds good on paper, but is absurdly paced and surreal in reality. You meet random people, they say something crazy or nonsensical, and then off you pop, chasing the mission marker. The game simultaneously makes an attempt to justify why Ajay (the protagonist) is doing typical Far Cry one man army stuff, but the explanations are... lacking. There are a few meaningless/illusory decisions (Achievements will pop up saying "Decided X, Y, or Z's fate" and... I didn't decide shit!). The mystic sequences are a mixed bag, mostly not great, and fail to assert themselves as significant or meaningful enough not to feel like distractions. You fight a boss in a mystic sequence, and it would have been much, much more interesting to fight them "for real". In classic FC fashion, things happen to your protagonist in cutscenes that make them look incompetent or unaware, and it's cringeworthy, railroading writing but... I can't be more mad about it than I am for any FC game. 

Changing up your loadout to tackle missions is great! Not having many opportunities to do so, or even convenient weapons laying around based on what the next railroaded story segment is... not great. I ended up playing many sequences exactly 2 times: failing to something vaguely BS on the first, and then bringing a different kit/doing one thing different and getting through them trivially easily. It's like groundhog's day, except unsatisfying and thin. There are stealth-mandatory sequences, and yes, you can get through them with just sneaking + your knife but... I would have made the choice to bring silenced weapons if I knew it would be fail-on-detect, and not stealth suggested, like so many other sequences! Vice versa with any kind of vehicle destruction. Oh, you didn't bring a grenade launcher (which is a sidearm, for some reason?)... enjoy pelting the van with bullets, hope you don't run out! Oh you did bring it? Well, this should take about 10 seconds.

The ugly: This really got under my skin, maybe it doesn't really need its own category, but... (SPECIFIC SPOILER) there's a mission where you spot the main villain, chase them for... hm... two minutes? Then you blow up their escape car, killing them... except it was a body double! The villain is 'dead' for about 5 seconds, calling you on your phone immediately after the mission is over to gloat. So... what was the point of any of that? This body double isn't very important, his death doesn't change anything for our protagonist (no thoughts about killing someone who was probably forced to be a body double?), and the villain's absence has zero narrative or meta-narrative purpose. Great writing, team.

Far Cry 4 is an open-world first-person shooter set in the fictional Himalayan region of Kyrat. Players take on the role of Ajay Ghale, who returns to his homeland to scatter his mother’s ashes, only to get swept up in a civil war against the ruthless dictator Pagan Min.

The game excels in providing a massive, beautiful open world filled with diverse landscapes, from snowy mountains to lush jungles. The combat is fluid and varied, allowing players to use a wide range of weapons, vehicles, and even wildlife to tackle objectives. The dynamic world and side missions keep the gameplay engaging, while the story provides a solid backdrop to the chaos.

However, Far Cry 4 doesn’t stray too far from its predecessor, Far Cry 3, with much of the gameplay and mechanics feeling similar. The main story can feel a bit generic at times, and some players may find the repetitive side activities and mission structures to be formulaic. Additionally, Pagan Min, while memorable, doesn’t quite have the same depth as past villains.

Far Cry 4 is a fun and action-packed experience for fans of open-world shooters, but it doesn’t innovate much beyond Far Cry 3.

At first, the game felt like it had potential. But just under 6 hours I had had too many hiccups with it and could not see myself baring anymore. If you think that's too short time to form an opinion, please just skip this review: it is mainly venting.

Positives included that the game introduced a multiple possible story lines. When you decide, which action to take, you can't do the other action. Sounded promising. Also, the main villain seemed kinda cool (I did found the characters in FC3 mainly either boring or annoying).

Negatives then, oh boy.

- If you fail a mission, you often have to repeat cut scenes. Cut scenes cannot be skipped.
- If you jump out of a vehicle, it may just keep going. Like, for a long time.
- Shooting enemies often resulted in them flying 30 feet up in the air. Which, I guess, is not the usual happenstance when you shoot someone to the head.
- The main character seems to be boring as they come. But, it may be because I didn't play the story long enough.
- The amount of animals roaming the map seemed pretty sweet at first. Encounters with them or other hostile enemies happen often. But combined with the fact that you have to travel a lot on foot or by a vehicle during missions and between them, this becomes tiresome really soon.
- Did I mention that you have to travel a lot manually? Hey, there's a feature for autopilot in vehicles if you're on a bigger road. Except the autopilot is totally malign: it drives you straight against hostile vehicles, doesn't care if there's rubble on the road, does sometimes drive you just wherever.
- Map is just mainly confusing. It might be a me problem, but I have seen much easier ones. Maps are supposed to help navigate the world and this didn't seem to do it very well.
- Win-key does not let you out of the game. Ctrl+alt+del doesn't let you out of the game. Only thing that lets you out of the game is the built-in feature for exiting the game, which isn't available when you are in the cut scene or when the gam is loading.

The straw that broke this camel's back was that I was in middle of a mission, without knowledge that the online is a bust. I called for a online player to help me get through a battle I had found difficult and already had tried couple of times. When they left (without actually showing during the battle), the game threw me back where I started the mission. Again, there was the same unskippable cut scene and kilometre of trecking through the game map. When travelling to the battle, if you'd died, it was back to the cut scene before trying again. A nuisance.

So yeah, the game is broke. But I'll reserve myself a chance to give it a go again if it's never remastered. Until then, consarn you , Ubisoft.

I'm so torn about this game. I sort of like it...it's also kinda boring. I'm really on the fence but I wouldn't recommend it. Also, the Ubisoft Connect launcher is required.

It's a well made game. All the mechanics are solid. I haven't hit any bugs or even any inconsequential jankiness. 

I just feel like I'm going through the motions already and I'm only 25 hrs in.

I was really excited about the hunting and skin gathering. Then it just became drop bait, predator instantly rushes in, a couple shotgun blasts to the face, gather skin and bait, repeat. There's no tracking or stalking unless you impose limits on yourself. Killing animals with your bow or knife will yield double the skins but it's way faster to just drop bait and shotgun blasts them for the single skin because you can complete that cycle in 4 or 5 seconds. That's really not an exaggeration at all.

The injections are a cool idea but there are very few herbs. Green, Yellow, Red, Blue, Purple, and White. Green gives you the HP injections and the other 3 injections are a combination of two of the other herbs. I honestly don't feel like I ever need them except the HP ones. The one that tracks all wildlife and enemies around you is very useful but it makes much of the game trivial.

I really like the bow to stealthily take over an outpost! I would set up on the highest point I could find near the outpost and use the camera to tag enemies and spot the alarm boxes. I'd usually have to find different vantage points to get a good understanding of the enemies present and where the alarms are located. Then I'd get close and snipe one or two enemies before racing off to another hiding place and picking off more. It is a really fun way to take over a place.

However, it becomes stale and you can simply fire multiple RPGs at them and snipe with a gun or run in with damage reduction injections, all enemies tagged, faster run (with auto-dodge) and wreck the place.

It's one of those games I feel like I should love but it's a slog at best. 

Looting enemies and chests will give money or literal vendor fodder. So, just money. I can't spend it fast enough. It's entirely meaningless.

The collectable are very basic. The masks are sort of neat. A marked area will show up near you and you need to follow the sound to find the mask and destroy it. Sadly, it's really boring too. The grappling hook is actually pretty cool with some neat physics-based swinging. Like most of the mechanics, though, it get's old really quickly. I feel no real incentive to explore.

The skills are nothing new but not the most basic I've seen. The "trees" are actually just ~10 linear paths with 5 skills each (most are passives). I have skill points into a bunch of stuff I never use because the 3rd or 4th node is actually something I want. For the most part, I don't have anything I want to invest in. 

I paid <$10 CDN so I don't feel like I got ripped off. I just don't feel compelled to keep playing.

Far Cry 4 on PC is like riding a yak off a cliff: wild, unpredictable, and probably fatal to your save file.
------------------------------------------------
🔹Story Quality:
Great setting with solid villains (Pagan Min is memorable) Typical Far Cry structure, not particularly groundbreaking hallow moral choices. Surface-level worldbuilding. The story takes a backseat to the action.

🎮 Controls:
The controls are solid, but the experience on PC can feel clunky at times. Keyboard and mouse might feel a bit too sensitive for some actions, and there’s no real “feel-good” fluidity compared to the console version. the aiming and the vehicle controls are the most common complaints.

🌍 Immersiveness:
The setting is gorgeous, but the immersion is hampered by bugs and performance issues. The rich Himalayan world should be breathtaking, but constant crashes and stuttering make it difficult to lose yourself in the experience. There’s a sense of adventure, but it’s constantly interrupted by technical issues. Plus, the lack of the original music adds to the immersion problem.

⚔️ Difficulty:
Far Cry 4’s difficulty feels off. The game can be too easy at times, but there are difficulty spikes that seem out of place. It feels more like a pacing issue than anything; the first few hours are relatively smooth, but then it can get frustrating quickly. **Co-op makes it a bit unbalanced, since only one person can progress in the campaign.

🗺 Level Design:
While the world is large and filled with things to do, it’s marred by repetitiveness. Missions feel like filler, and unlocking stuff on the map feels more like a grind than an engaging challenge. Repetitive side-quests and scattered collectibles can make it feel like you’re running in circles a lot.

🎨 Graphics:
The game looks great overall, especially considering it’s from 2014. The environments are beautiful, from lush forests to the snowy mountains of Kyrat. The textures can get blurry at times, especially in the distance, but overall, the visuals hold up. PC optimization is a mess. The graphical bugs, like stuttering and occasional pop-in, definitely break the immersion.

🎵 Sound and Soundtrack:
The soundtrack was once one of the standout features of the game, Ubisoft ruined it with a patch. The lack of ambient music in key areas takes away from the experience, and even the updated soundtrack doesn’t quite capture the same vibe.
Sound effects are solid, but not enough to make up for the missing music

🕹 Gameplay:
Core gameplay is still fun, with a mix of shooting, driving, and exploration that keeps things fresh. But the constant crashes, save file issues, and broken co-op make the experience a lot less enjoyable than it should be. Co-op: Feels like a missed opportunity. You can’t do anything meaningful with a friend unless you’re wandering the open world.

🐛 Bugs:
This game is riddled with issues. From save file corruption to constant crashes and soft locks, it’s clear that Ubisoft didn’t prioritize PC optimization after launch. Graphical glitches, weird physics, and a broken co-op system.

⌛ Playtime:
~30-50 hours, depending on how much you’re trying to 100% the game. If you’re just rushing through the main story, it might be quicker, but if you get sidetracked by all the side activities, it could stretch to 50+ hours.

🔁 Replayability:
 The open world is large and full of things to do, but once you’ve played through the story and finished the main objectives, there’s not much else to keep you coming back. Co-op: Doesn’t offer much incentive, since your progress in the open world doesn’t carry over.

💰 Price: 
Far Cry 4 is often discounted, so it’s worth picking up at a low price. But at full price, the technical issues might make you regret your purchase. I Wouldn’t pay more than: $10 for the PC version unless it’s been heavily patched, which we know it hasn’t.

The Good Stuff:
✅ Engaging gameplay, especially the open world and shooting mechanics.
✅ The world design and variety of locations is impressive.
✅ Co-op, if you can ignore the limitations, can still be fun for exploration.
✅ Fun outposts and collectibles for completionists.
✅ Steam achievements

The Bad Stuff:
❌ Terrible PC optimization: crashes, soft locks, and graphical issues.
❌ Misleading co-op “campaign” promises – a huge letdown.
❌ Broken ambient music, and updates that only make things worse.
❌ Constant game-breaking bugs and save file issues.
❌ The "new content" feels like a distraction from fixing long-standing issues.
------------------------------------------------
💬 Conclusion:
Far Cry 4’s PC version is a frustrating experience. Despite its stunning world, solid shooting mechanics, and great design, the technical issues are too much to overlook. The lack of proper co-op and ruined soundtrack further diminish the potential of what could’ve been a solid game. Until Ubisoft fixes these issues or offers some real optimizations, you're better off playing this on console or waiting for a sale. It’s a mess, but it’s still fun in short bursts – if you’re brave enough to fight the bugs.

Beware that the game is extremely particular with controller support.  You need to literally unplug your mouse and keyboard and launch the game in big picture mode to get a controller to work.  Far Cry 3 had an option in the settings to turn a controller on and off.  I think they just straight up forgot to put that in the controller settings. But with all of that aside, the game has much better mouse and keyboard controls than Far Cry 3 did imo.  The weapon wheel comes up instantly and is very intuitive unlike 3's clunky and slow weapon wheel and just everything in general feel tighter and better to play.  Button prompts actually work almost 100 percent of the time unlike 3 where i find myself dying too often just from not being able to heal or loot ammo despite holding the button down for seconds on end.  I hear some people knocking the grappling in this game but personally I've never had a problem with it and quite enjoy it.  Gone are the days in Far Cry 3 where you're attempting to climb a mountain by simply getting lucky and hoping you don't slide back down.  Maybe I'm just stupid and suck but I find it much more enjoyable to scale massive cliffs grappling from point to point.  Green Leaves were overly common in Far Cry 3 to the point where you can pick up at least 6 heals at pretty much any place in the map.  This is not the case in 4 and I honestly like it.  It's too easy in FC3 to stack heals and just bull charge in to a lot of fights and just abuse them til all the enemies are dead.   FC4 also adds an actual waypoint path which is a small but extremely welcome addition.  So many times in FC3 I would have to open and close the map over and over just to find where I needed to go.  I don't mind this in Far Cry 2 since you don't have to pause the game to look at the map but it gets old after a while on a first playthrough of 3.  There's more changes that I didn't mention but for the most part, it's just more Far Cry 3.  Which isn't a bad thing I'm always down for more FC3 in different locations.  Keep in mind that this game was made in 9 months.  Which means there are some drawbacks to this game.  The world of Kyrat is beautiful and wingsuiting through the landscape will never get old.  But when you get up close with the world, it can show how rushed it was built.  The most common and obvious example is all the grass on uneven ground often floats far above the ground.  Its nothing that strongly impacts the game negatively but it does get annoying when you're sneaking around the bushes finding the best way to take on an outpost or fortress.  I also don't think the story is nearly as meaningful as FC3.  Don't get me wrong I still really enjoy the story but Pegan Min is nothing compared to Vaas.  That's all I'm gonna say about the story to avoid any possible spoilers cause I still feel its worth playing.  Hunting animal skins is so much better in FC4.  Thanks to the improvements to the bow.  You get double skins for clean kills on animals which is from killing them with either the knife or the bow.  I found that in FC3 the bow was pretty much useless.  I could never get kills on enemies unless it was a perfect head shot.  And when I say perfect I mean PERFECT.  Maybe I just have the worst luck on the planet but I never used the bow after my first time trying it.  In FC4 I make sure I always have the bow in my inventory.  I love taking out entire outposts with it.  The more intuitive weapon wheel also makes the bow much more usable with it being much faster to switch arrow types.  It's not the most effective weapon I could have but it's so much f*****g fun to use I just don't care.  Now the main reason I bought this game.  The Co-op mode.  I'm not even gonna compare it to FC3's dumpster fire of a Co-op mode because it's no comparison.  It is a bummer that you can't play campaign missions in Co-op other than the fortresses but DO NOT sleep on this game's Co-op.  Me and my friend played it for 10 hours straight and cleared out literally every possible thing on the first half of the map all in one sitting.  It is insanely fun.  It is a must buy when it goes on sale for 5 dollars and you and your friends are bored.  There isn't much more to talk about with this mode, well there is but I've been typing this for 2 hours and I want to wrap this up so I can play this game more.  The last thing I want to talk about is the performance.  In my personal experience, the game runs a lot better than FC3.  FC3 still runs fine and I would not say in any way that it's unplayable but FC4 on the highest settings runs significantly better than FC3 on the highest settings.  Keep in mind that this is my personal experience but I found the game to be much more stable and smooth.  Which is really impressive considering the world is more dense than Far Cry 3's.  This brings me to the end of my review.  I still think Far Cry 3 is a better game than 4.  That might just be nostalgia talking but I found the game to just flow much better than 4.  FC4 definitely has better overall gameplay than 3 but I feel like 4's story likes to jump around a lot more with having multiple paths to take in many missions and there's almost always more than 1 campaign mission available at a time.  This isn't a bad thing but it can make the story a bit harder to follow.  There are times I'm not even sure what the point of the mission is.  Far Cry 3 never gave me this issue.  Aside from the beginning of the game I always knew the reason behind every mission.  Alright, I'm burnt out on typing.  Play Far Cry 3 first if you haven't.  It is a little harder to go back to 3 with some of the additions that 4 has but you don't notice the issues on the first playthrough.

**Coming back as a Far Cry fan with adult money and the power to write a review**

I start off very strong like every Far Cry game, but I get bored quickly. 

**Frustrating - Tedious - Ages Badly**

No matter how much I dislike this franchise and its developers, I always find myself coming back for more, hungry for that Ubisoft formula. 

I absolutely adore Far Cry 3, despite its gameplay aging poorly, because the story was strong enough to keep me engaged (just ignore the side content; you won’t miss out on much, to be honest). 

However, with this game, it feels tedious to play. I don’t know why, but everything about it frustrates me and gives me the feeling of "I'm just trying to get through this game and be done with it." 

There are no story set pieces that captivate or immerse me. The gameplay feels recycled and is starting to show its age, which makes it hard to stay engaged without a compelling story to hold my interest. 

But credit where it’s due: the setting is beautiful. I love the statues and the original soundtrack; they did an excellent job there. The game is incredibly grindy for the cool weapons; I feel like I spent about 25% of my playtime hunting and grinding for the signature weapons, which is boring and repetitive. This makes the gameplay loop dull early on. 

The Sri Lanka set pieces were decent but also demonstrated poor game design and were tedious to play through. 

It feels like a reskin (albeit a very well-done reskin; I love the aesthetics) of the main game, dropping you into some mystical location where you have to navigate the area with a bow and arrow and some light traversal mechanics. 

I wish they had developed the story of Kyrat more, focusing on the architecture and soundtrack, rather than just making the player shoot things all the time, which would make exploration more enjoyable. 

Driving has improved significantly and feels more fluid, but the sloppy hills can sometimes make it frustrating to drive, forcing you to take the "correct" path the game intended, which creates annoying moments. 

Not to mention, the game runs poorly on modern hardware (even with 8-core setups), making it a pain to replay.

I don’t know—I'm just fed up with this developer. I'm not even that familiar with the mainstream criticism against them, but maybe they're right.

Well. Not really my cup of tea, I suppose. I mean I got it for less than a tenner because I wanted some brainless FPS action, and that's what I got, but that's as far as the game goes, really. Has all the problems of FC3, in fact it's really just the same game only with different graphics. Haven't tried FC5 or 6, because now I have a strong reason to believe they are also the same exact game only with different graphics.

Pros: 
Scenery is pretty
No silly monsters or anything like that as enemies
"open world"

Cons:
The world is open, but really just empty. You can't hope to find anything truly interesting anywhere, so why bother exploring? Also the world looks exactly the same everywhere, so after the first 15 minutes you've seen it all even if you've only seen 5% of the actual map area. 

The characters are just extremely caricaturish and shallow, everyone has like 2 lines of dialogue and that's as deep as their personalities go. The main villain initially comes across as a totally out-of-control psychopathic homicidal maniac (who for some reason talks and dresses like some London Soho gay TV-personality), and the big plot twist is that there isn't any. He remains just as homicidal psychopath all the way to the ending, and if the game is trying to give you some mixed feelings about him it's failing badly.

There's quite few different guns and weapons in the game, but because they are all more or less equally good, you just end up choosing one or two and sticking with those, so then you'll have like 27 others which you never have to touch.

There's like half a million 'side quests' available in the world, but they are all completely pointless since all they give you is money and xp, and you don't really NEED either to progress through the main story line.

You can buy some 'perks' with the xp, but they're all completely pointless so after a while you just can't be arsed anymore, and you have 35 skill points unused, and half of the available perks unselected. 

The main story line takes about that 30 hours to complete, not even that if you never bother with any side quests and stuff. It offers no real surprises or really anything truly impressive story-wise.

So in conclusion, if you just want to shoot at some human enemies AND the game happens to be in a big discount, then maybe yeah, otherwise naaaah.

Far Cry 4 is... fine. Everything is accessible, simple, and easy to understand. It's your typical FPS Open World game, nothing more, nothing less. The gameplay is copy-paste from Far Cry 3. No groundbreaking mechanics, no innovations. A vast, beautiful open world that somehow feels lifeless, empty, and artificial.

Gunplay is identical to Far Cry 3. A ton of weapons to choose from, but you'll just end up using a silenced pistol for one-shot headshots or a grenade launcher to blow up vehicles. Stealth? Same old stuff. Traversal? Boring as always. Enjoy driving for minutes on end to reach repetitive, uninspired missions. Watch a cutscene, then drive more. Rinse and repeat until the credits roll.

The AI is delightfully brain-dead. Enemies and allies alike seem to exist only to ruin immersion. They'll run straight into your line of fire like they’ve been programmed to lose. Zero challenge, zero life, just the perfect Ubisoft charm.

Now, the villain is decent. Interesting personality, compelling worldview, and charismatic. But everyone else? Boring. Well, Amita’s pretty, so she’s at least visually engaging. Too bad her role and dialogue are as dull as the rest. The story progression is painfully slow and filled with nonsensical character motivations. Go destroy this, kill that—like you’re some kind of errand boy for an entire nation. Immersion is non-existent. You’re just a one-man slave army in a story that takes itself way too seriously.

The game is fun for the first 30 minutes. After that? You’ve seen it all. There’s no twist, no surprises, no “wow” moments. Exploring the open world? Don’t bother. Tons of activities and collectibles, but they’re as enticing as watching paint dry. The rewards is just spare change and XP you don’t even need to finish the game. If you’re not a completionist, skip it all.

Oh, and the narrative pacing? A disaster. The game pretends there’s something urgent going on, but then casually suggests you go hunting, climb mountains, or drive around. Sure, let’s just ignore the world-ending stakes for some hiking. Honestly, the best ending is waiting still in the room and eating Grab Rangoo. Makes more sense than the entire campaign.

Performance is weirdly bad. Far Cry 5 and 6 run at over 100 FPS on my rig, but this one struggles to hit 70, regardless of settings. Feels like the game didn’t get the memo about modern hardware.

If you’ve never touched a Far Cry game, you might enjoy this one. But if you’ve played any FPS games before or more than one Far Cry title. It’s the same thing all over again, just with a new map and story. And I’m beyond bored!

Very similar to Far Cry 3...just bigger and buggier!! An absolute mess of a game!!

Graphics haven't aged that well, kinda rough looking BUT it's enough to enjoy a play through. You'll have some nice moments but the lighting just feels off and travelling in the buzzer at a height just shows how bad the engine runs. 

Animals are crazy!! They are more of a threat than the armed humans!! Chaos all the time. People screaming to be saved from eagles at almost every place you stop at. Constant gun fire and mess...not a lot of chill time and a healthy portion of jank thrown in too!! Inputs don't register, lots of graphical glitches in lighting and shadows, constant attention seeking from the game be it people shouting or animals attacking. 

I approached one tower and during the time it took me to liberate it I was attacked by 3 honey badgers, 3 eagles and a pack of wolves whilst managing constant gun fights from passing grunts. It was absolute chaos and made me remember how near impossible it is to concentrate on any one thing at a time. You will suffer the longer you stand in one place. It just never ends. Sure kids will find it fun but adults do want to a sense of completion when playing and having all of your hard stealth work thrown away can be really frustrating. The intelligent game design found in gems like Dishonoured is no where to be seen in any of the missions offered in Far Cry 4.

Sabal and Amita are a joke. You have to choose which one of them to help but no matter what you do the other one will always shout at you and will hate you for not going with them. You go and complete some side missions and they'll come on the radio saying "Yeah not bad but you're not helping enough people." It's just so un-rewarding when the writers thought that throwing these emotions at you would be fun. It's not and not being able to help people and get good vibes from it just adds to the overall pointless feeling these games give. The illusion of choice when it's just a load of low value busy work.

And something that many modern games love doing is here to ruin the game-play with long running animations for climbing, landing, reloading and healing. Playing on the hard difficulty and towards the end of the game you will be in fight after fight. Once you're out of healing injections you're victim to the manual heal. This animation goes on forever. Add to that the reload animation and you'll find yourself running around like a headless chicken begging for the fight to pause so you can make time to watch the incredibly annoying healing and reload animations. You cannot do anything quickly at this point and it's nothing short of a nightmare...

Minus one point for pushing the UBI launcher on us. And another one for not letting players skip cut-scenes!! They all go on for way too long and characters talk so much rubbish I always used the time to go get a drink.

Some helpful tips that will save you some research:

Posters and masks can't always be reached so use guns or explosives/fire to destroy them
There are bee's nests on towers (that's what's hurting you!!) Be(e) sure to break the nests!!
Hear hissing?? Snakes are nearby and they're next to invisible so use your cross hair. It'll turn red when you're aiming at them.
Go into your general options in game and turn off the looting animation!

5/10 - Absolute chaotic mess and full of jank that'll ruin all the fun BUT it's still playable and isn't a bad game. If you've got nothing better to do it'll certainly help to burn some time.
